stem:
What does this code print?

count = 0
while count < 3:
    print(count)
    count += 1
explanation_after: A while loop keeps running as long as its condition is True. count starts at 0, prints, then increments: prints 0 (count becomes 1), prints 1 (count becomes 2), prints 2 (count becomes 3) — now count < 3 is False, so the loop stops. Output: 0 1 2.

break immediately exits the loop entirely, skipping any remaining iterations. i takes values 0, 1, 2 and prints each. When i becomes 3, the if condition triggers break before print(i) runs, so 3 is never printed and the loop ends. Output: 0 1 2.

The outer loop repeats over the whole dataset multiple times (epochs); the inner loop iterates over the smaller batches within a single pass through the data
The inner loop exists only to print progress messages
Nested loops are a Python syntax requirement for all training code

explanation_after: Training data is usually too large to process all at once, so it's split into batches. The inner loop walks through every batch once — that's one epoch. The outer loop repeats that entire process multiple times, since a model typically needs to see the data many times to learn well. Two nested loops directly mirror the two concepts: epochs (full passes) and batches (chunks within a pass).
